question.text: Ms. Priya Shah has been proposed as Trustee for the Satpura Market-Neutral Fund, a Category III AIF structured as a trust. Which of the following would DISQUALIFY her from acting as Trustee under SEBI (AIF) Regulations?

answer.text: She holds a CFA charter but not a CA qualification.
She is simultaneously serving as an independent director of the Investment Management Company of the same AIF.
She is a resident Indian but not an NRI.
She has less than 5 years of experience in asset management.

explanation.text: The Logic: The regulations explicitly bar the trustee from being the manager, director (including independent director), officer, or employee of the investment management company. This avoids conflicts and preserves the trustee's fiduciary independence. There are no explicit qualification, residency, or experience floors prescribed for trustees in SEBI (AIF) Regulations 2012. The Trap: Option A invents a CA-only rule that does not exist. Option C is irrelevant. Option D is a plausible but non-existent experience cutoff. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C tests the same trustee-independence rule across categories. XIX-D tests it with Cat I/II framing. Mutual fund trustees (X-A/X-B) have a stricter independence rule under MF Regulations. Manager's Pro-Tip: If your proposed trustee has ANY directorship link to the IM company, the PPM filing will bounce. Run a 'trustee crosswalk' during PPM drafting: list every trustee company director and cross-check against the IM company's board and senior officers. Fix before merchant-banker certification, not during SEBI comment cycle.
